samples.summary: The change's central re-framing ("client read-only mounts are a correctness boundary, not access control") is recorded only in notes.md and yorkie-auth-webhook.md; the canonical share-link doc still asserts the opposite
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sharing.md:208-217` still states: "in the default one the client-side `readOnly` flag **is the write boundary** rather than a convenience in front of one. That is why the client-side gates are treated as load-bearing throughout this document…", and `docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:299-300` repeats it ("the client `readOnly` flag is the effective write boundary for an anonymous viewer whenever the Yorkie auth webhook is left in shadow mode"). This change adds the contrary statement in `docs/design/notes/notes.md` ("An earlier draft … claimed that … the proxy *is* the write boundary on a default install. That was wrong") and in `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md` ("they are correctness boundaries, not access control, and no feature should be reviewed as if they were"). Repo doc discipline is to fold a correction into the canonical subsystem doc rather than leave two answers; sharing.md is the share-link doc and is where every reviewer of a viewer-role feature will look. Cost stays inside the codebase (contradictory guidance), so minor — but it is exactly the kind of divergence that led to the wrong claim being repeated in the first place.

samples.summary: The identical wrong claim survives in the docs package's read-only wrapper doc comment, which the new notes wrapper explicitly contradicts
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42`: "the server-side check behind it — the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default …, so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one." `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:53-70` (added here) says that reasoning "was wrong" and states the opposite for the sibling module. Two sibling modules now document opposite security postures for the same mechanism; the change corrects only the new copy.

samples.summary: ~90% of the read-only Proxy (traps, memoization, batch, non-configurable-descriptor exception) is copied from packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts rather than shared, and the two copies already differ
samples.evidence: Compare `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:75-185` with `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67-169`: the `get`/`set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`isExtensible`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` traps, the memoization map, the non-configurable-non-writable escape hatch and the `batch` special case are line-for-line equivalent, differing only in the reader allowlist plus notes' new additions (`HISTORY_METHODS`, `READ_ONLY_VIEWS` idempotency). The generic half is engine-agnostic (it only needs a reader allowlist and a per-member policy) and could live in `@wafflebase/core`, which the repo's reuse expectation points at; `docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:46-48` lists *store abstraction unification* as a Non-Goal, which covers the interfaces but not this trap machinery. The concrete cost is drift in a security-relevant boundary: the notes copy is idempotent and returns `null` from `undo`/`redo`, the docs copy does neither, so a trap hardening applied to one will not reach the other.

samples.summary: The frontend mount wraps the store read-only even though the engine's initialize() now wraps it too — a layering divergence from the docs precedent, and the reason the idempotency WeakSet had to be invented
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:248` already does `const store = readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(noteStore) : noteStore;`, mirroring `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1075` (`readOnly ? readOnlyDocStore(docStore) : docStore`). In docs, only the engine wraps — `docs-view.tsx` hands over the raw store. Here `notes-view.tsx:151-152` wraps first and passes the wrapper in, which is what forces `READ_ONLY_VIEWS` (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:41-46) to exist purely to make double-wrapping a no-op. Only `getText()` for the thumbnail is read through `storeRef` (notes-view.tsx:183), so the frontend wrap buys nothing the engine wrap does not already give; the extra layer plus its bookkeeping is scope the docs pattern shows is unnecessary.

samples.summary: Backend webhook changes (boot-time posture log, `target=` added to the shadow-deny log) are unrelated to the share-link notes-parity outcome and ride along in this change
samples.evidence: The stated outcome of this change (per docs/design/notes/notes.md § Share-link parity and the issue it cites, #1044) is that the share-link note route mounts the toolbar and behaves like the workspace route. `logPosture()` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:117-140) and the `target=` addition to the shadow-mode warning (line 156-161) change deployment observability of the auth webhook rollout, a separate subsystem with its own design doc; nothing in the notes parity work depends on them (the notes doc only *references* the log line). It is small, tested and doc'd in docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md § Risks, so the cost is review surface rather than behavior — but it is unrequested scope in a frontend-parity change and would be cleaner as its own commit.

samples.summary: Divider hit-area (7px → 25px) and `touch-action: none` are an unrelated engine-level UX change bundled into the parity fix, and the same change removes the case that motivated them
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:286-303` widens the divider and adds `touch-action: none`, plus a `track` recalculation at line 538. The motivation given ("a fingernail on a phone … made the split read as fixed there") is a phone concern, yet the same change makes both mounting routes demote `both` → `edit` below the mobile breakpoint (notes-detail.tsx:119, shared-notes-layout.tsx:56-57), so the split is no longer offered on a phone at all. The remaining benefit is tablet/desktop pointer ergonomics — a legitimate but separate fix from the share-link parity outcome, and it alters shared engine geometry for every route.

samples.summary: Reusing the docs share-token uploader drops the workspace route's user-visible upload-failure feedback for share-link editors
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:40-49) returns `Promise<string>` and throws on failure; the notes `UploadImage` contract (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:19-26) expects `null` to mean "the host already told the user". The workspace route wraps upload in a handler that toasts every failure (notes-detail.tsx:208-231). On this new mount a rejected upload is only swallowed by the engine's `failed()` handler (image-upload.ts:179-188), which logs to console and removes the ghost, so a share-link editor whose image upload is rejected (size, type, network, 403) sees the placeholder vanish with no explanation. Note SharedDocsLayout has the same gap, so this follows an existing precedent rather than inventing one — but the parity claim in docs/design/notes/notes.md ("the paste/drop/pick path behaves as it does for a member") is not quite met.

samples.summary: Uploader gating diverges from the sibling docs share layout without the divergence being called out
samples.evidence: shared-notes-layout.tsx:56-57 gates on `token && !readOnly`, while SharedDocsLayout (shared-document.tsx:326-334) deliberately does not gate on `readOnly` and documents why ("the backend refuses a viewer-role token, so `readOnly` here is a UI decision, not the gate"). Both are defensible; having the two share surfaces answer it differently is a small consistency cost.
